text:
Jackson LaCombe is playing 27:08 a night, the kind of ice time reserved for a team's No. 1 defenseman, and the Ducks are treating him like one. He has 19 points in 17 games, a nine-game point streak (all assists), and 11 power-play points from the first unit.

The points are padded. Anaheim has scored 8.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and its five-on-five chance share with him out there is 38.3 percent, more than ten points worse than without him. That is an ugly number for a top-pair defenseman, and some of it comes with facing other teams' best players for 27 minutes.

Last season tells a kinder story. Evolving-Hockey rated him 46th among 215 defensemen with 1.5 wins above replacement, with his team creating more with him on the ice (94th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.4 primary shot assists per 60, 98th percentile among defensemen. The Eden Prairie native, a 2019 second-round pick out of the University of Minnesota, can move the puck. Watch the five-on-five share: it should rise, but the assist pace should fall.
headline: LaCombe's minutes are huge; his on-ice numbers aren't
